title: Esther 6
paragraphs: ¹ That night the king could not sleep. He ordered the book of records — the chronicles — to be brought and read aloud to him. ² It was found recorded that Mordecai had exposed the plot of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the doorway, who had plotted to assassinate King Ahasuerus. ³ "What honor and recognition has Mordecai received for this?" the king asked. His attendants answered, "Nothing has been done for him." ⁴ The king asked, "Who is in the court?" Haman had just arrived in the outer court of the palace to speak to the king about having Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built for him. ⁵ The attendants replied, "Haman is standing in the court." "Bring him in," the king said.

⁶ So Haman entered, and the king asked him, "What should be done for a man the king wishes to honor?" Now Haman thought to himself, "Who would the king want to honor more than me?" ⁷ So Haman answered, "For a man the king wishes to honor, ⁸ have them bring a royal robe the king himself has worn and a horse the king has ridden, one with a royal crest placed on its head. ⁹ Let the robe and horse be given to one of the king's most noble princes. Let him robe the man and lead him through the city square on the horse, proclaiming before him, 'This is what is done for the man the king wishes to honor!'" ¹⁰ "Excellent!" the king said to Haman. "Hurry — take the robe and the horse just as you have said, and do exactly this for Mordecai the Jew who sits at the king's gate. Do not leave out a single detail."

¹¹ So Haman took the robe and the horse, dressed Mordecai, and led him through the city square on horseback, proclaiming before him, "This is what is done for the man the king wishes to honor!" ¹² Afterward Mordecai returned to the king's gate. But Haman rushed home in a panic, his head covered in shame. ¹³ Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had happened to him. His wise men and his wife Zeresh said to him, "If Mordecai — before whom your downfall has begun — is of Jewish descent, you cannot prevail against him. You will only continue to fall before him." ¹⁴ They were still talking with him when the king's eunuchs arrived and hurried Haman away to the banquet Esther had prepared.
